event: The anjiawenda.com domain lapses or is lost, and every installed copy of Pexi stops reaching its server.
trigger: Registration runs out on 2027-08-19 (Cloudflare is the registrar, paid through that date). The ACT notes say auto-renew was to be turned off, and that was still an open action on the date written. Pexi's own docs say the owner and renewal date are unknown.
cost: Total outage for all users until a new app build passes App Review (days). The address is baked into the app at build time and there is no remote setting to repoint it. Domain itself costs roughly US$10 a year (assumed, derived from ACT notes).
detect: Nothing watches the registration date. The first sign would be the outage alarm after the domain stops resolving.
response: 1. Log in to the Cloudflare account that holds the domain and renew for several years. 2. If it already lapsed, buy it back in the grace window. 3. If lost, ship a build with a new address.
smallest_fix: Log in to Cloudflare, confirm auto-renew is ON (the ACT plan may have switched it off) or pay for 5 years now, and put the date in his calendar.
sources: C:\ACT\NOW.md:20-22; C:\ACT\docs\decisions.md:2665-2667; native/scripts/sync-web.mjs (injects SHIN_API_BASE); mac/config.env.example; docs/readiness/BRIEF.md:33-34

event: Cloudflare (tunnel, DNS, TLS) goes down, suspends the free account, or changes the free tunnel terms, so the phone cannot reach the Mac.
trigger: Cloudflare outage; account or abuse suspension; free-plan change; tunnel credential revoked. On 2026-11-18 17:50 UTC the public health address answered 530 (tunnel unreachable) per the mailbox, and an earlier 530 raised the GitHub alarm at 02:42Z.
cost: App down for every user for the length of the problem. Scans fail, Plus is not checked, no estimates. A suspension also takes the domain (item 01) and the email forwarding with it.
detect: GitHub server-alarm probes every 30 minutes and emails after two failures; Lookout checks health every minute but only alerts a Windows PC; the deploy checker mails the PC. All three have fired on a real 530.
response: 1. Check the Cloudflare status page and the Mac tunnel job. 2. Restart the tunnel job on the Mac (remote over Tailscale). 3. If the account is suspended, appeal and in parallel stand up another tunnel host.
tried: yes: detection worked on real 530s, 2026-11-18 02:42Z (carryover-lookout.md:99) and 17:50 UTC (mailbox message); no written recovery steps
smallest_fix: Write a 6-line recovery note (who can restart the tunnel, where the tunnel credential lives, where to appeal) and put it in mac/README.md. Note the app has no second address to fail over to.
sources: mac/README.md (Cloudflare one zone, Free plan, tunnel shin-beta); .github/workflows/server-alarm.yml:1-70; C:\dev\lookout\server\src\expected.ts; mailbox message 20261118175032-mac-37a71f; C:\agent\.claude\state\carryover-lookout.md:99

event: The Apple Developer Program membership is not renewed on time, and the app is removed from sale and updates stop.
trigger: Yearly fee due around 2027-10-08 (enrolled 2026-10-08). Card declined, or web enrollment does not auto-renew (Apple's page states auto-renew only for app enrollment). What Apple does on lapse is not confirmed (assumed: app removed from the store).
cost: Pexi disappears from the App Store for new downloads and subscriptions cannot be sold. Fee is about CA$149 (assumed).
detect: Apple emails the account holder before expiry (assumed). No calendar item or checklist found for it.
response: 1. Renew in the developer account. 2. Confirm the payment card is current. 3. After a lapse, renew at once and re-submit if the app was removed.
smallest_fix: Calendar reminder for 2027-09-08 and a check of the renewal setting and card in the developer account now.
sources: RULINGS.md:540-570 (enrolled 2026-10-08, individual); https://developer.apple.com/support/enrollment/ (checked 2026-11-18, lapse behaviour not stated)

event: Apple suspends the developer account, rejects an update, or pulls Pexi from the store.
trigger: Guideline or privacy-label problem (the privacy policy mismatch on RevenueCat was found and fixed; ML Kit disclosure is unproven), an account flag, or an unanswered App Review message.
cost: All new users and all subscription revenue stop. The seller is Jamin's own legal name and Apple refuses business-name accounts, so it is a personal account. Appeals take days to weeks (assumed).
detect: Apple emails the account holder and shows a banner in App Store Connect. Who reads that email and how fast is not written down.
response: 1. Read the Resolution Center message the same day. 2. Fix and resubmit, or appeal with the review notes. 3. Aurik answers French and testing questions.
smallest_fix: Add Aurik as an App Store Connect user so a second person sees review messages, and write a one-page 'if Apple rejects' note linking the review notes.

event: A fix cannot be built or uploaded because the Apple signing set-up has quietly expired or broken.
trigger: The Xcode account session already vanished within days once (2026-11-04 to 11-07), so builds sign with an App Store Connect API key. The distribution certificate and profile are created at export and expire yearly (assumed). The key can be revoked. Only one Mac has Xcode, and it is also the server.
cost: A bad bug, a store-requested change or a privacy fix cannot ship for however long the set-up takes to repair (hours to days).
detect: Only when someone tries to build. Nothing checks the certificate date or the key.
response: 1. Re-create the certificate through the API key path. 2. If the key is revoked, make a new one in App Store Connect. 3. Follow native/README.md build steps.
tried: yes: 2026-11-08, build 4 uploaded with the API key; build 9 on 2026-11-17
smallest_fix: Put the certificate expiry date and the API key location in the calendar, and run one dry build each quarter.
fix_cost: 20 minutes plus one 30-minute build each quarter

event: Apple raises the minimum Xcode, SDK or iOS requirement and the Mac cannot build for it, or Google ML Kit raises its iOS floor and drops older iPhones.
trigger: Apple yearly SDK requirement for uploads (assumed from past practice, not checked this session). Xcode 27.1 on macOS 27.0.1 with 27.2.1 pending. Deployment floor is iOS 16.0 and was forced by GoogleMLKit 8.0.
cost: Updates blocked until the Mac is upgraded; or a raise of the floor excludes users still on older iPhones (size unknown).
detect: Apple email or an upload error at build time.
response: 1. Read the Apple notice and date. 2. Update macOS and Xcode on the Mac. 3. Rebuild and upload.
smallest_fix: When Apple announces the next SDK date (usually spring), put the build in the calendar one month before. Keep macOS current.
fix_cost: 10 minutes now, about 2 hours when it happens

event: A macOS update restarts the Mac and the server does not come back until someone logs in.
trigger: Auto-install of updates is on. The server is a login-session job (LaunchAgent), and the plist itself says a reboot needs auto-login or the server stays down. Whether auto-login is on was not found. FileVault (finding D1) disables auto-login when switched on.
cost: Full outage for as long as the Mac sits at the login screen; Jamin remote login needs Screen Sharing or SSH, which may not be up before login.
detect: GitHub alarm and Lookout would see health fail; the cause would not be obvious.
response: 1. Log in to the Mac (screen sharing or physically). 2. Confirm the jobs started. 3. Set auto-login or move the server to a system-level job.
smallest_fix: One reboot drill: restart the Mac while watching the alarm and write down whether the server came back unattended. Decide this together with the FileVault choice.
sources: mac/launchd/com.shin.server.plist (header comment about reboot and auto-login); docs/security-check-mac-2026-11-16.md; docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md:49-53

event: Apple holds payouts or blocks sales because agreements, tax forms or Canada paperwork are missing or out of date.
trigger: A new Apple agreement to accept, a tax or bank change, the GST/HST number condition for Canadian-resident developers, or the 'Part XX Canada compliance: Missing Info' item that was listed and never resolved in the notes.
cost: Subscription revenue held or the paid-apps agreement shows inactive so purchases fail. Size is the month's subscription income.
detect: Apple email and a banner in App Store Connect. No scheduled look at the Agreements page.
response: 1. Open Agreements, Tax and Banking. 2. Accept or complete what is flagged. 3. Check IAP products show Ready to Submit.
smallest_fix: Open the Agreements page once now to clear Part XX and see the GST status; then look again on the first of each month.
sources: docs/launch-gaps-2026-11-06.md:198-202 (Paid Apps, tax forms, bank Active; Part XX unknown); docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md:71 (F4); docs/security-check/legal-review-2026-11-17.md

event: RevenueCat is down or slow, so paying users are treated as free and cannot buy or restore.
trigger: RevenueCat outage or slow responses. The server check has no timeout, caches a good answer 10 minutes and a failure 60 seconds, and on a failure with no cached answer returns not-Plus without logging. The phone side throws when the store is unreachable and shows Try again.
cost: Once weekly limits are switched on (they are off now, finding C1), every paying user would be cut to 10 scans a week during an outage, and a hung call could stall a scan. Churn and refund requests, size unknown.
detect: Nobody would know. The server swallows the error and nothing alerts.
response: 1. Check status.revenuecat.com. 2. Keep known Plus users on Plus until it returns. 3. Look for stalled scans.
smallest_fix: Add a 3-second timeout, log every failure, and keep a user who was Plus in the last 24 hours as Plus on any error.
sources: app/src/scan-quota.ts:140-278 (isPlus, cache, no AbortSignal); app/public/js/purchases.js (loadPlans, refreshPlus); docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md:43 (C1)

event: The RevenueCat secret key is rotated, revoked or mistyped on the Mac, and every paying user quietly becomes a free user.
trigger: Key rotated after a leak (the breach plan says to rotate it), account change, or an edit error. The server warns at start only when the key is empty, not when it is rejected.
cost: Same as item 09 but permanent until noticed: paying users capped on the free allowance once limits are on.
detect: Nobody would know. A rejected key produces the same silent not-Plus.
response: 1. Make a new secret key in the RevenueCat dashboard. 2. Put it on the Mac and restart the server. 3. Test with a known Plus device.
response_exists: yes: docs/privacy/breach-plan.md:37 (menu names assumed, not checked)
smallest_fix: Have the server check the key once at start and every hour, put the result in the health page, and make the alarm fail on it.

event: RevenueCat changes its API, retires the v1 endpoint Pexi calls, or ends the free tier.
trigger: Vendor change. Free until US$2,500 a month tracked revenue, then 1% of tracked revenue (checked 2026-09-23). The server uses the v1 REST address.
cost: The 1% is written down as a known cost. An API retirement would act like item 10 (all Plus users read as free). Notice would go to the RevenueCat account email.
detect: Vendor emails to the account holder (assumed). No one reads that on a schedule.
response: 1. Read the vendor notice. 2. Switch the server call to the new endpoint. 3. Deploy and test with a Plus device.
smallest_fix: Make sure the RevenueCat account email is one he reads, and add the pricing line to the cost list.

event: The Claude price estimate stops working (Anthropic outage, empty credit balance, key revoked, billing lapse) and shoppers silently get no range.
trigger: A 401 or a 'credit balance too low' error counts as a model failure and takes a cap slot; the breaker opens after 5 failures for 60 seconds. Shoppers wait at most 6 seconds, then see no estimate. Reasons are stored in the scan row and a log file.
cost: Products with no known price lose their estimate, so fewer scans end in a verdict, hurting trust and paywall conversion. Direct spend is small (worst case about US$9 a month per the security check).
detect: Nobody would know unless Jamin reads the scan rows or error log. The health page carries only the monthly-cap flag.
response: 1. Look at Anthropic status and the console balance. 2. Top up or replace the key on the Mac and restart. 3. Check the next scan gets a range.
smallest_fix: Count recent model failures in the health page, make the alarm fail when the last 20 calls all failed, and turn on low-balance email in the Anthropic console.
sources: identify/src/range-ask.ts; identify/src/provider.ts (classifyProviderError); app/src/distribution.ts (onceAsk); app/src/catalogue-first.ts:1166-1199; price/src/estimate.ts:148; docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md:24

event: Anthropic retires the model Pexi calls or changes the API, and every estimate call fails.
trigger: Pexi uses claude-haiku-4-5-20251001, listed Active with a tentative retirement 'not sooner than October 15, 2026' (that date has passed with no retirement announced). Anthropic promises at least 60 days email notice. The 2026-10-21 API version removes temperature and similar settings, and Pexi sends none.
cost: Same as item 12 from the day of retirement; estimates gone until a deploy.
detect: Anthropic email to the console account (assumed reader). The deprecations page is not watched.
response: 1. Read the notice and date. 2. Change the model id and deploy (push to main). 3. Check one estimate.
smallest_fix: Confirm the Anthropic console email is one he reads, and add a quarterly look at the deprecations page to the calendar.

event: Growth uses up the 1,000 calls a month Claude cap early and estimates stop for the rest of the month with no push alert.
trigger: A viral spike, or one caller using the shared allowance. The cap counts before sending. When reached the server writes a log line at most hourly and sets a flag on the health page. The brief says the cap alerts loudly; in code it is a log file line and a flag, which the alarm does not read.
cost: Up to 30 days without estimates exactly when many new users arrive. Raising the cap costs cents (worst case about US$9 a month at current volumes).
detect: Only the log line or someone reading the health page.
response: 1. Raise the cap setting on the Mac. 2. Restart the server. 3. Check an estimate returns.
smallest_fix: Make the alarm fail when the health page says the cap is reached, and set the cap in proportion to users with a note of its monthly cost.

event: Open Food Facts throttles or bans the Mac's address, and scans of barcodes missing from the local catalogue end with no name.
trigger: OFF allows 15 product reads a minute per address. Pexi's server makes the calls from one address for everyone, sends no custom User-Agent, and the OFF page says it may ban by address. Also 503 under OFF's global load.
cost: Shoppers on new barcodes are asked to type the name; a launch spike would hit this first. Reads still work for the 121,949 rows already in the catalogue.
detect: The server logs a loud 'SCAN ENDED WITH NO NAME' line per scan, in a file nobody reads; no alert.
response: 1. Check the error log for off_failed counts. 2. Email OFF with the contact and the fix if banned. 3. Slow the live lookups and rely on the local catalogue.
smallest_fix: Send a proper Pexi User-Agent with a contact email, and cap live OFF lookups at about 12 a minute with a queue.
sources: app/src/open-food-facts.ts (4s timeout, 2,000 entry cache, no User-Agent); app/server.ts (logNoName, ~line 1780); https://openfoodfacts.github.io/openfoodfacts-server/api/ (checked 2026-11-18)

event: OpenStreetMap Overpass blocks Pexi, slows down or goes away, and the nearby-shops list is empty.
trigger: The public overpass-api.de server is volunteer run and says to expect low reliability. Its guidelines count all users together, ask for an identifying User-Agent, and ask commercial apps to self-host. Pexi sends the User-Agent 'shin-beta (price scanner, six testers)'.
cost: Store chooser empty, so shoppers cannot tag a shop; prices lose location. The code fails soft and returns an empty list with a 5-minute empty cache and a 24-hour cache per area (memory only).
detect: Nobody would know. Failures are swallowed.
response: 1. Point the setting at another Overpass mirror. 2. Restart the server. 3. Check the store list in the app.
smallest_fix: Correct the User-Agent to name Pexi with a contact, and write down one fallback mirror address.

event: The Project Hammer download moves, is renamed or stops being published, and prices go stale.
trigger: The weekly job downloads one zip from a single person's site. A missing or renamed file fails the job. Prices cover one Toronto neighbourhood and Hammer is the main price source (98,918 observations).
cost: Verdicts slowly drift from real prices; trust loss. The job fails loudly and the alarm fires after 8 days.
detect: GitHub alarm checks the last refresh is under 8 days old, so up to 8 days late.
response: 1. Check the source site and the refresh log. 2. Ask the author or find a new address. 3. If it is gone, keep the last load and say nothing new is coming.
smallest_fix: Write the 3-step response and keep a copy of the last good download on a second disk.

event: A bad or changed Hammer file loads cleanly and puts wrong prices in front of every shopper.
trigger: Truncated zip, shifted columns, zero or absurd prices, or a stale copy re-published. The import does not check row counts, newest date or price drift, and marks the data refreshed anyway, so the alarm proves only that Pexi's job ran.
cost: Wrong 'great price' verdicts at scale until someone notices; the worst trust event in the angle. A poisoned price also has no removal tool (finding B3).
detect: Nobody would know.
response: 1. Restore the previous catalogue from the nightly backup. 2. Mark Hammer withheld until fixed. 3. Reload after the file is inspected.
smallest_fix: Refuse to load when rows drop more than 30% from last time, the newest day is over 14 days old, or median price moves over 25%.

event: The other data sources age quietly with nothing to say so, and prices and product facts drift.
trigger: BC Liquor (June 2026 list), StatCan (newest 2026-09), Open Prices (874 observations), Open Beauty, Pet and Products Facts and the OFF, USDA and Icecat dumps have no scheduled refresh and no staleness alarm.
cost: Gradual loss of accuracy; low per day, adds up over a year. Open Facts rows are only a fallback so impact is small.
detect: Nobody would know. Only the Hammer refresh has a freshness alarm.
response: 1. List each source's last load date. 2. Reload the ones that matter (liquor and prices). 3. Withhold any source judged too old.
smallest_fix: Put each source's last-loaded date on the health page and alarm on the two price sources.
sources: app/src/attribution.ts (sources and counts); mac/launchd (only backup, checker, hammer, server, tunnel jobs found)

event: A source sends wrong rows (a vandalised product name, a bad price) and there is no quick way to remove them or switch the source off.
trigger: Crowd-edited OFF names or images, a Hammer or Open Prices error, or a source owner asks to stop use. A withhold list exists in code (anbl, walmart.ca, returnit, consignaction are withheld), but removing single bad rows has no tool.
cost: A wrong name or price stays in front of shoppers until Jamin edits a database by hand; requests from a data owner could sit unread (see item 24).
detect: Shopper correction or a support email, if anyone reads it.
response: 1. Add the source to the withhold list and deploy to hide it. 2. Delete the bad rows by barcode. 3. Reply to whoever reported it.
tried: yes: withheld retailer sources already in use (anbl, walmart.ca, returnit, consignaction)
smallest_fix: One script that hides a barcode or a source by name, and a written 3-line procedure beside it.
sources: app/src/attribution.ts; docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md:37 (B3: no way to remove a poisoned price)

event: GitHub suspends the personal account or the Pages site goes down, and the Terms and Privacy links in the App Store listing and the app go dead.
trigger: Account suspension, a Pages outage, a repo rename. The legal pages live at xu826jamin.github.io/pexi (terms, privacy, support), on Jamin's personal account, and nothing monitors them.
cost: A dead privacy URL is an App Review problem and can get the app pulled; legal pages are also needed for the subscription flow.
detect: Nobody would know. The alarm probes the server only.
response: 1. Restore the Pages site or move the pages to another host. 2. Update the links in App Store Connect. 3. Check the in-app links.
smallest_fix: Add the three legal URLs to the GitHub alarm so a 404 emails him, and keep a copy served from the Pexi server too.

event: The GitHub outage alarm itself stops running, so a real outage is not emailed.
trigger: Included Actions usage on GitHub Free for private repos is US$12 a month, about 2,000 minutes at the Linux rate (my arithmetic). The alarm runs 48 times a day and each failing run waits 90 seconds, so 1,440 runs a month use at least 1,440 and perhaps 2,900 minutes if each is billed as 2. Whether the repo is private was not confirmed. Schedules can also be delayed, and a suspended account stops them.
cost: No outage email while the allowance is spent; blocked at month end if no card is on file. Lookout covers only while the PC is on.
detect: Nobody would know if it stops; GitHub emails at 90% usage if a payment method is on file.
response: 1. Make the repo public or move the probe to a cheaper schedule. 2. Check Actions usage in billing. 3. Run the probe by hand once to confirm email.
smallest_fix: Check the repo is private or public and the month's usage in GitHub billing, and if private, switch the schedule to hourly or add a dead-man check from outside.

event: GitLab goes down, or the Mac's deploy key is revoked, and Jamin cannot ship a fix.
trigger: GitLab outage, account action, SSH key rotation. The deploy checker polls GitLab every 30 seconds; when it cannot reach it, it keeps the last fetched copy and logs one line. The GitHub mirror exists (origin pushes to both) but the checker does not use it.
cost: Live server keeps running. A fix during an incident cannot deploy until access returns. No customer data impact.
detect: The log line only; no alert, and nobody would see a fix not arriving until they tried.
response: 1. Check GitLab status. 2. Point the Mac's stage copy at the GitHub mirror. 3. Deploy and point back.
smallest_fix: Write the 3-step 'deploy from the GitHub mirror' note and try it once.
sources: mac/deploy/checker.mjs:28-42; git remote -v (origin pushes to GitLab and GitHub); mac/README.md; mac/DEPLOY.md

event: The support inbox (useshinapp@gmail.com) goes unread or the Google account is suspended, and Apple, privacy-request or customer messages are missed.
trigger: Nobody is named as reader. Apple App Review, a data deletion request with a legal deadline, a refund question and a data owner's request would all arrive there. Gmail suspension or long inactivity closes it.
cost: Missed legal deadlines on privacy requests (fine) and unanswered Apple messages (store removal risk); users who write and hear nothing do not stay.
detect: Nobody would know a message arrived.
response: 1. Check the inbox weekly. 2. Answer privacy requests with the data-requests procedure. 3. Forward Apple mail to Jamin at once.
response_exists: yes: docs/privacy/data-requests.md (how to answer a request; nothing on who watches the inbox)
smallest_fix: Forward the inbox to Jamin and Aurik and add a Friday check to the weekly routine.
sources: docs/readiness/BRIEF.md:48-49; docs/store/listing.md; RULINGS.md:540-570 (support email only useshinapp@gmail.com); docs/privacy/data-requests.md:1-13

event: Tailscale access to the Mac expires or the free plan changes, and Jamin cannot fix the server from away.
trigger: The Mac's SSH and Screen Sharing are reachable only on the home network and Tailscale. Device keys expire by default (180 days, assumed). The Lookout PC link over Tailscale is also not yet set up.
cost: After May 2027 Jamin is at a full-time internship; an outage that needs a hands-on fix would last until he is at the Mac.
detect: Nobody would know until he tries to connect.
response: 1. Re-authenticate the Mac in the Tailscale admin page. 2. Switch off key expiry on that node. 3. Test from outside the home network.
smallest_fix: Turn off key expiry on the Mac node and log in from a phone hotspot once.
sources: docs/security-check-mac-2026-11-16.md (SSH and Screen Sharing on LAN and Tailscale 100.112.113.11); C:\dev\lookout\docs\server-proof.md:73; C:\dev\lookout\docs\PLAN.md:19

event: The Lookout alert path breaks (ntfy.sh down, PC asleep, Healthchecks ping not set) and only the GitHub email remains.
trigger: Lookout runs on the Mac, alerts through ntfy.sh to Windows notifications on the PC, and its dead-man ping to Healthchecks is optional (whether set was not found). When the PC is off or ntfy.sh is down, no page is shown.
cost: Slower discovery of an outage: only the GitHub email (after two failed half-hours) is left.
detect: The 530 on 2026-11-18 raised the GitHub alarm and the mailbox report; Lookout's own page is PC-only.
response: 1. Check the GitHub email and the mailbox for the outage message. 2. Open Lookout on the PC when it is on. 3. Check Healthchecks for the hub ping.
response_exists: yes: C:\dev\lookout\docs\PLAN.md (hub watched by a Healthchecks check)
tried: yes: 2026-11-18, two real 530s detected through GitHub and the mailbox
smallest_fix: Confirm the Healthchecks ping address is set on the Mac and that its email reaches a mailbox he reads.

event: CocoaPods' package list goes read-only on 2026-12-02, so no new ML Kit, RevenueCat or Capacitor iOS pods can be published or picked up.
trigger: Date announced by CocoaPods. Existing versions keep installing. Pexi is on CocoaPods because the ML Kit barcode and text plugins ship no Swift Package Manager file.
cost: After that date a security update or an Apple SDK-driven fix in an iOS pod cannot be shipped; possible loss of the barcode scanner at the next forced Xcode change. Timing not known.
detect: Nobody would know; it surfaces when a build breaks.
response: 1. Keep the current pod set and rebuild from it. 2. Check whether the plugin vendor added Swift Package Manager support. 3. If not, plan a scanner replacement.
smallest_fix: Keep a copy of the current Pods folder and lock file on a second disk and re-check plugin Swift Package Manager support in January.

event: Apple or Google raise a privacy question about ML Kit (disclosure, data manifest, telemetry), and the build is flagged or a policy edit is forced.
trigger: Finding E4: the privacy manifest needs the Mac's pods and the real build to prove complete. ML Kit may need a disclosure.
cost: A rejected submission delays launch by days; wrong disclosure risks the App Store listing.
detect: Apple's upload checks or an App Review message, which is a late warning.
response: 1. Generate Xcode's privacy report on the archive. 2. Fix the manifest and the policy wording. 3. Resubmit.
smallest_fix: Run the privacy report on the real archive on the Mac once, and fix anything it lists before the public submission.

event: A build-time download source (npm registry, GitHub-hosted packages, CocoaPods CDN, the embedding model) is unreachable or changed, so a deploy or rebuild fails.
trigger: npm outage, a yanked package, or the embedding model file lost with the Mac disk. The server crashes seconds after starting without the model file, which lives only in the deploy overlay on the same disk as the live data.
cost: A deploy that fails is refused and live stays untouched (safe). The model file loss would leave the server unable to start after a disk loss; backups sit on the same disk.
detect: A refused deploy posts to the mailbox; a lost model would show as a crash loop on the alarm.
response: 1. Read the deploy refusal in the mailbox. 2. Retry later for an outage. 3. Restore the model from a copy kept elsewhere.
response_exists: yes: mac/DEPLOY.md (refuse and keep live; overlay location)
tried: yes: 2026-11-17 deploys proven working (BRIEF.md:36-37); registry outage not tried
smallest_fix: Copy the embedding model and overlay folder to a second disk or cloud storage once and say where in mac/DEPLOY.md.
sources: mac/DEPLOY.md (overlay and embedding model lines); mac/deploy/deployer.mjs:5; docs/security-check/FINDINGS.md:50 (D2)

event: A service credential leaks or a vendor is breached, and the keys on the Mac must be replaced at speed.
trigger: Vendor breach, a stolen Mac (FileVault is off), or an accidental commit. Keys involved: Anthropic, RevenueCat secret, admin token, the Cloudflare tunnel credential, the App Store Connect key, GitLab and GitHub access. A leaked Anthropic key could spend credits outside Pexi's own cap, which only counts calls made through the server.
cost: Unwanted spend on the Anthropic balance, forged Plus status, or a hijacked tunnel; and a breach notice duty.
detect: Vendor email, an unexpected bill, or an alarm; not watched.
response: 1. Revoke and re-issue the key in the vendor dashboard. 2. Update the Mac and restart. 3. Follow the breach plan for notices.
response_exists: yes: docs/privacy/breach-plan.md:28-50 (rotation table; menu names assumed)
smallest_fix: Rotate one real key as a drill (start with Anthropic) and set a monthly spend limit in the console.

event: A vendor changes terms or privacy position (Apple, Anthropic, RevenueCat, Cloudflare, Google) and the published privacy policy no longer matches.
trigger: Terms update emails; Quebec s.17 wants an assessment and agreement for each recipient outside Quebec (Cloudflare, Anthropic, RevenueCat), which is not done. The policy already mismatched on RevenueCat once and was fixed.
cost: A policy that misstates what is sent is an App Store and fine risk. Size not known (lawyer question).
detect: Vendor emails to the account owners; nobody reviews them on a schedule.
response: 1. Read the change. 2. Update the policy and Apple privacy labels. 3. Ship an updated build if the labels changed.
smallest_fix: List the vendors and the date each page was last read, and re-read the five pages every quarter.

event: A free tier ends or a price rises for a small service Pexi leans on (Cloudflare tunnel, Tailscale, Healthchecks, ntfy, GitHub minutes, Anthropic tokens).
trigger: Vendor pricing change. Examples: RevenueCat 1% past US$2,500 a month, GitHub minutes (item 22), Anthropic per-call price.
cost: Small money each, but a surprise stops a service: a tunnel plan change would be a full outage.
